audit.title: Supported Networks (Chainlink Functions)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Each network subsection is self-contained (router + DON ID + endpoints + billing), good for per-network lookups. Weak: no opening summary that answers "which networks does Functions support?" in one liftable sentence/table, and the deprecation status is not in liftable text.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. 1 H1, clean H2→H3 per network, 0 level skips, 36 focused tables, median 93 words/section — near-ideal RAG chunking.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Exact addresses, hex DON IDs (36 hex identifiers), fees in "cents USD", LINK thresholds. The "0 with units" measurement is a detector artifact — cells carry units inline.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Block-explorer links per address are useful and authoritative; 0 links to primary spec/canonical concept pages (e.g. what a DON is, billing spec). Acceptable for config, but definitions aren't attributable.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The USD-fee NOTE is crisply quotable. No one-line definition of "Functions router," "DON ID," or "premium fee" near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags, head metadata uncapturable. For a reference page whose value is freshness of addresses, missing last-updated is a real trust gap.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No fenced blocks; addresses live inside `<Address>` components that render as UI, not copy-pasteable config. An agent scraping the `.md` gets URLs but no clean address/DON-ID config object.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "router address on X" / "DON ID for X" via per-network headings. Missing symptom/how-to phrasing ("what's the gateway endpoint for encrypted secrets", "is Chainlink Functions deprecated") and any overview/FAQ.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clean and consistent. Minor: "1 requests" (Soneium/ZKSync mainnet) grammatical slip; per-network NOTE blocks are heavily repeated.

audit.summary: This is a config-reference page listing Chainlink Functions router addresses, DON IDs, gateway endpoints, and billing parameters across 11 networks (mainnet + testnet). Its dominant strength is dense, extractable specifics — 162 numerals and 36 tightly-scoped tables, one coherent chunk per network. Its biggest opportunities are (1) surfacing the **shutdown status** — currently rendered only as an invisible `<ChainlinkFunctions callout="shutdown" />` component, meaning engines cannot lift the single most important fact on the page — and (2) missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates) plus the absence of an answer-first overview table naming all supported networks.

recommendations.title: Surface the shutdown/deprecation status as liftable text
recommendations.issue: critical status is invisible to text extractors — component renders nothing in the `.md`.
recommendations.change: add a plain-text sentence immediately below the H1, e.g. "As of {date}, Chainlink Functions is [deprecated/being sunset]; new subscriptions on {networks} are {status}." State it verbatim, dated.
recommendations.why: engines answering "is Chainlink Functions supported/deprecated?" will otherwise hallucinate from priors; the highest-severity fact is currently unretrievable.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first overview table of all supported networks
recommendations.where: directly after the intro, before "## Arbitrum"
recommendations.issue: no single chunk answers "which networks does Chainlink Functions support?"
recommendations.change: insert one summary table: Network | Mainnet? | Testnet | Router address | DON ID. Lead with the canonical list in the first liftable sentence: "Chainlink Functions is supported on 11 networks: Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, Celo, Ethereum, OP, Polygon, Soneium, ZKSync…"
recommendations.why: captures the highest-volume query with a self-contained, quotable unit instead of forcing engines to synthesize across 28 sections.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD + visible last-updated date
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, canonical URL; render a visible "Last updated: {date}" line.
recommendations.why: for address/fee data, freshness is trust; dated, schema-tagged pages are preferentially cited and this page controls none of it today.

recommendations.title: Provide agent-runnable config, not just UI components
recommendations.where: each network section or an appendix
recommendations.issue: addresses are locked inside `<Address>` components; no copy-pasteable block.
recommendations.change: add a fenced JSON/YAML block per network (or one combined block) with `router`, `donId`, `donIdHex`, `gatewayUrls`, chain id. Tag the language.
recommendations.why: coding agents can then lift a complete config object; raw `.md` currently yields prose-embedded values only.

recommendations.title: Add one-line canonical definitions near first use
recommendations.issue: "Functions router", "DON ID", "premium fee" used without definition.
recommendations.change: add crisp definitions with inline links to the billing/architecture canonical pages, e.g. "The Functions router is the on-chain contract you send requests to; the DON ID identifies the Decentralized Oracle Network fulfilling them."
recommendations.why: gives engines verbatim-liftable definitions and attributable primary references.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to phrased headings or a short FAQ
recommendations.issue: no coverage of natural-language queries beyond the address-lookup pattern.
recommendations.change: add H3s like "What is the encrypted-secrets gateway endpoint?", "How much does a Functions request cost on {network}?", "Which testnets are supported?"
recommendations.why: matches how devs/agents actually query and wins retrieval that table-only content misses.

recommendations.title: Fix "1 requests" grammatical slip
recommendations.where: Soneium Mainnet and ZKSync Mainnet billing tables
recommendations.why: minor fluency correction; consistency aids clean extraction.

antiPatterns: Critical status hidden in a non-text component (`callout="shutdown"`) — invisible to extractors.
Repeated identical NOTE block across all 11 networks — acceptable redundancy for chunk-independence, but consider a single canonical statement plus per-section reference.
No stale-content signal — undated page whose value is time-sensitive address/fee data.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is referenced at the top — good site-level signal; verify it lists this page.
Metadata (JSON-LD, canonical, dates) could not be verified from served HTML; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a definitive read, but measured facts confirm none present in the served markup.
Address values are rendered by client-side components (`client:load` / `client:only="preact"`); confirm server-rendered fallbacks exist so non-JS crawlers and agents see the addresses.
